title: The Poisson Limit Theorem: Multinomial Converges to Independent Poissons
description: Proves the Poisson limit theorem (law of rare events): as n→∞ with n·pₙ→λ, the binomial pmf converges to the Poisson pmf e^(-λ)·λ^k/k! = poissonPMFReal λ k. The joint version shows a multinomial distribution converges to independent Poisson components, the asymptotic-independence statement asked for by the parent's open question.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. All 7 theorems are fully machine-checked with 0 sorries; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool).

overview.historicalContext: The Poisson limit theorem, also called the 'law of rare events' or Poisson's law of small numbers, was published by Siméon Denis Poisson in 1837 (*Recherches sur la probabilité des jugements*). It states that the binomial distribution Binomial(n, p) approaches the Poisson distribution with rate λ when n is large and p is small, with np→λ — modeling the count of rare events among many independent trials. The multinomial generalization shows that several rare event types, observed jointly, become asymptotically independent Poisson variables; this underlies the Poisson approximation to contingency tables and the theory of point processes. Mathlib defines `ProbabilityTheory.poissonPMFReal` but contains no theorem connecting it to the binomial limit, so this fills a genuine gap.
overview.problemStatement: As the number of trials n→∞ and the per-trial success probability pₙ→0 with n·pₙ→λ, does the binomial pmf C(n,k)·pₙ^k·(1-pₙ)^(n-k) converge to the Poisson pmf e^(-λ)·λ^k/k!? And does the joint multinomial pmf converge to a product of independent Poisson pmfs?
overview.text: Proves binomial_tendsto_poisson: for fixed k, C(n,k)·pₙ^k·(1-pₙ)^(n-k) → e^(-λ)·λ^k/k! whenever n·pₙ→λ; restates it against Mathlib's poissonPMFReal; and proves the joint multinomial_tendsto_prod_poisson: the multinomial pmf over a finite set of 'rare' cells (with an implicit residual cell) converges to ∏ᵢ e^(-λᵢ)·λᵢ^{kᵢ}/kᵢ!, i.e. the cells become asymptotically independent Poissons.
overview.proofStrategy: Decompose the binomial pmf into three independently convergent factors. (1) C(n,k)·pₙ^k = (1/k!)·∏_{j<k}((n-j)·pₙ); each falling factor (n-j)·pₙ → λ since n·pₙ→λ and j·pₙ→0, so the product → λ^k. (2) (1-pₙ)^n → e^(-λ) via Mathlib's Real.tendsto_one_add_pow_exp_of_tendsto applied with g n = -pₙ. (3) (1-pₙ)^(n-k) → e^(-λ) because it equals (1-pₙ)^n/(1-pₙ)^k eventually and (1-pₙ)^k → 1. For the joint version, the key product limit ∏_{j<K}(n-j)·∏ᵢ(pᵢ n)^{kᵢ} → ∏ᵢ λᵢ^{kᵢ} is proved by rewriting the falling factorial as n^K·∏(1-j/n) and regrouping into ∏ᵢ(n·pᵢ n)^{kᵢ}, avoiding any explicit pairing bijection; the residual factor (1-∑pᵢ)^(n-K) → e^(-∑λᵢ) = ∏ᵢ e^(-λᵢ) supplies the exponential terms.
keyInsights: The whole proof reduces to three convergent factors multiplied together — the only Mathlib input beyond elementary limit algebra is Real.tendsto_one_add_pow_exp_of_tendsto for (1+g n)^n → e^t.

The falling factorial / probability pairing is handled without a bijection: ∏_{j<K}(n-j)·∏ᵢ(pᵢ)^{kᵢ} = ∏_{j<K}(1-j/n)·∏ᵢ(n·pᵢ)^{kᵢ}, because n^K = ∏ᵢ n^{kᵢ} distributes across the cells (Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum).
Asymptotic independence is encoded in the residual exponential: (1-∑pᵢ)^(n-K) → e^(-∑λᵢ), and e^(-∑λᵢ) = ∏ᵢ e^(-λᵢ) factorises to give exactly one e^(-λᵢ) per cell.
p→0 is not assumed separately — it follows from n·pₙ→λ since pₙ = (n·pₙ)/n and the denominator tends to ∞.
The result is stated against Mathlib's poissonPMFReal so it plugs directly into the existing Poisson distribution API.

sections.title: Module Overview and Proof Strategy
sections.summary: States the open question (the Poisson limit / law of rare events), the three-factor proof strategy, the Mathlib gap (poissonPMFReal exists but no binomial→Poisson convergence), and lists the status checklist.

sections.title: Auxiliary Limits
sections.summary: tendsto_zero_of_tendsto_nat_mul (n·pₙ→λ ⟹ pₙ→0), tendsto_one_sub_pow_exp ((1-pₙ)^n → e^(-λ) via Real.tendsto_one_add_pow_exp_of_tendsto), and tendsto_one_sub_pow_sub_exp (the shifted factor (1-pₙ)^(n-m) → e^(-λ) for any fixed m, reused by both the one-cell and joint theorems).

sections.title: The Poisson Limit Theorem (one cell)
sections.summary: binomial_tendsto_poisson: the binomial pmf → e^(-λ)·λ^k/k!, assembled from the three convergent factors. binomial_tendsto_poissonPMFReal restates the same limit against Mathlib's ProbabilityTheory.poissonPMFReal with an ℝ≥0 rate.

sections.title: The Bijection-Free Product Limit
sections.summary: tendsto_descFactorial_mul_prod: ∏_{j<K}(n-j)·∏ᵢ(pᵢ n)^{kᵢ} → ∏ᵢλᵢ^{kᵢ}, proved by rewriting the descending factorial as ∏_{j<K}(1-j/n)·n^K, regrouping n^K into ∏ᵢn^{kᵢ} (Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum), and combining the two convergent factors — no explicit pairing bijection between cells and factorial terms is needed.

sections.title: Joint Limit: Multinomial → Independent Poissons
sections.summary: The multinomialPMF definition (s-many rare cells plus an implicit residual cell of probability 1-∑pᵢ) and multinomial_tendsto_prod_poisson: the joint pmf → ∏ᵢ e^(-λᵢ)·λᵢ^{kᵢ}/kᵢ!, assembling the product limit above with the residual exponential tendsto_one_sub_pow_sub_exp to give the asymptotic-independence statement.

conclusion.summary: The main results binomial_tendsto_poisson and multinomial_tendsto_prod_poisson prove the classical Poisson limit theorem and its multinomial generalization: a binomial converges to a Poisson, and a multinomial converges to independent Poissons, when the per-cell expected counts n·pᵢ converge to finite rates λᵢ. The one-cell limit is stated against Mathlib's poissonPMFReal. All 7 theorems are machine-verified with 0 sorries and depend only on the foundational axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
conclusion.implications: This supplies the missing convergence bridge between Mathlib's binomial machinery and its Poisson distribution. The Poisson limit theorem justifies the ubiquitous Poisson approximation for counts of rare events (defects, arrivals, mutations, rare-disease incidence), and the multinomial version is the foundation of the Poisson approximation to contingency tables and the construction of Poisson point processes from binomial thinning.
openQuestions: Strengthen pointwise pmf convergence to convergence in total variation (Le Cam's inequality: the total-variation distance between Binomial(n,p) and Poisson(np) is at most n·p²), giving an effective error bound rather than just a limit.
Lift the limit from pmfs to the measure level, proving the binomial measures converge weakly to poissonMeasure λ and the joint multinomial measures converge to the product Poisson measure.

crossReferences.description: Proves that each marginal of a multinomial is binomial; its third open question asks exactly for this Poisson limit.
The multinomial MGF/PGF framework on which the multinomial pmf used here is based.
The other classical limit law for the binomial: CLT gives the normal approximation for fixed p, while the Poisson limit governs the rare-event regime np→λ.
